title: wiper linkage
description: A crank, a coupler rod and a pivoting arm turn steady spinning into a back and forth sweep; no car, motor wiring or water shown

facts.intro: Introduce a recognizable wiper linkage: a red crank on the left, a steel coupler rod, and a long arm with a dark blade pivoting on the right over a pane of glass. Everything is still.
facts.cutaway: A simplified cutaway lifts the cover to expose the crank, the coupler rod joining it to the arm, and the pivot the arm swings on.
facts.drive: An illustrated push spins the crank a full turn. The coupler rod pushes and pulls the arm, which swings across the glass and back.
facts.response: The crank keeps turning and the arm keeps swinging. The crank goes all the way round, yet the arm only rocks back and forth through part of a circle.
facts.hold: No part moves for this explanation. The crank is the shortest link and can turn in a full circle; the arm is longer and can only swing.
facts.repeat: A second push turns the crank again, and the arm sweeps across the glass and back once more, covering the same arc each time.
facts.limit: The crank turns backwards for a moment. The arm retraces its path, because the rod ties every crank position to one arm position.
facts.payoff: The cover closes. Crank, coupler and arm work together: a steady spin becomes a sweep back and forth. No car or water is shown.

narration_rules.message: no car, rain or motor is depicted; speak only of the crank, coupler and arm
